questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain why sorting intervals by start time is necessary before merging them. Mention time complexity.

rubric.criterion: Explains that sorting aligns overlapping intervals contiguously in the array
Explains that without sorting, every interval would need pairwise checks taking O(N squared) time
States overall time complexity of O(N log N) dominated by sorting

questions.modelAnswer: Sorting intervals by start time places potentially overlapping intervals adjacent to each other. Without sorting, detecting overlaps would require comparing every pair against every other pair in quadratic O(N squared) time. Sorting takes O(N log N) time and enables merging in a single linear O(N) pass.

questions.prompt: In 2 to 5 sentences, explain why the merged end point must be calculated as max(last.end, current.end). Give an example of an enclosure where this is critical.

rubric.criterion: Explains that an earlier interval might completely contain or enclose a later interval
Provides a clear concrete example (such as [1, 10] and [2, 5])
Explains that assigning current.end directly would erroneously truncate the merged span

questions.modelAnswer: When two intervals overlap, the earlier interval might completely enclose the later one. For example, consider [1, 10] and [2, 5]. If you assign the end point directly to current.end, the merged interval becomes [1, 5], which loses the tail of the original span. Taking max(10, 5) keeps the correct span [1, 10].

questions.modelAnswer: The algorithm separates start times and end times into two arrays and sorts them independently. A start pointer and an end pointer track chronological event order. When a meeting starts before the earliest active meeting ends, an additional room is allocated. When an end time is reached, a room is freed, and the algorithm tracks the maximum rooms used.

questions.modelAnswer: Merging intervals requires sorting by start time so overlapping candidates appear contiguously in a single linear pass. In contrast, finding the maximum non-overlapping intervals uses greedy scheduling and sorts by end time. Picking the interval that finishes earliest frees up the timeline as soon as possible, leaving the maximum room for subsequent events.
